import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset

# Create a new column for the hour of the transaction

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots

# Create a bar plot for total sales by hour

sns.barplot(x='hour', y='total', data=data, estimator=sum, ci=None, palette='viridis')

# Set the title and labels
plt.title('Total Coffee Sales by Hour', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)

```python
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a new column for the hour of the transaction
data['hour'] = pd.to_datetime(data['date'] + ' ' + data['time']).dt.hour

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a bar plot for total sales by hour
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.barplot(x='hour', y='total', data=data, estimator=sum, ci=None, palette='viridis')

# Set the title and labels
plt.title('Total Coffee Sales by Hour', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
```
